areas.name: Umeda / Kita
areas.short: The main hub — shopping, offices, trains everywhere.
areas.long: Osaka's #1 desired area (SUUMO's top Kansai station 5 years running). Everything radiates from here.
areas.who: People who want maximum convenience and don't mind paying for it.
areas.expect: Department stores, Grand Green Osaka, endless dining, high rents, always busy.

areas.name: Nakazakicho / Nakatsu
areas.short: Indie cafes, vintage shops, creative — 5 min from Umeda.
areas.long: Nakazakicho is retro-cafe/creative; Nakatsu is residential but rising fast because it's just north of Umeda.
areas.who: Creatives and young pros who want a Tokyo-ish 'small streets near a big hub' feel.
areas.expect: Old townhouses turned cafes, galleries, a walkable low-rise pocket beside the Umeda towers.

areas.name: Fukushima
areas.short: Foodie heaven, lively at night, walkable to Umeda.
areas.long: Both modern-convenient and old shitamachi in character; Umeda is 1–2 stops or a walk away.
areas.who: Singles/couples who want restaurants and quick Umeda access.
areas.expect: Tiny izakaya-packed alleys, very livable, buzzing evenings without the tourist crowds.

areas.name: Nakanoshima / Kitahama / Yodoyabashi
areas.ja: 中之島・北浜・淀屋橋
areas.short: Classy riverside business district, tower condos.
areas.long: Feels like a polished Tokyo business zone — river views, museums, high-rises, few noisy streets.
areas.who: Higher budget; people who like clean, upscale urban living.
areas.expect: Kita-ku 1LDK rents ~¥135k; offices, cafes, riverside walks, tower mansions.

areas.name: Honmachi / Utsubo Park / Awaza
areas.ja: 本町・靭公園・阿波座
areas.short: Polished, central, calmer — a park makes daily life nice.
areas.long: Utsubo Park gives walks/cafes/dogs; Honmachi is very convenient for work but business-district-ish.
areas.who: People who want central but not nightlife-heavy — 'adult central Osaka'.
areas.expect: Office towers, a green park, tidy cafes, easy commutes across the whole metro.

areas.name: Horie / Shinmachi
areas.short: The coolest lifestyle area — design shops, boutiques, cafes.
areas.long: More stylish and relaxed than Namba/Shinsaibashi but still central; in higher-rent Nishi-ku.
areas.who: Younger professionals and creatives who want 'cool Osaka' without the chaos.
areas.expect: Interior/fashion shops, specialty coffee, wine bars, walkable and photogenic.

areas.name: Namba / Shinsaibashi
areas.short: Nightlife and chaos central — fun to visit, intense to live.
areas.long: Ranks high as a desired station, but living there is a very different experience from visiting.
areas.who: People who specifically want the buzz right outside their door.
areas.expect: Dotonbori crowds, shopping arcades, tourists, noise, ultimate convenience.

areas.name: Tennoji / Abeno
areas.short: Big-station convenience, family-friendly, more local.
areas.long: Known as a strong education district (HOME'S), with shopping, parks and older residential pockets.
areas.who: Families wanting big-station convenience without Kita/Minami chaos.
areas.expect: Abeno Harukas, Tennoji Park, zoo, schools, calmer residential streets nearby.

areas.name: Uemachi / Tanimachi 6
areas.short: Quiet, historic, tasteful — central but residential.
areas.long: Narrow streets, temples, older houses, cafes on the Uemachi plateau; less flashy.
areas.who: People who want to 'live in Osaka, not just near a station' but stay central.
areas.expect: Temples, antique/craft shops, calm streets near Osaka Castle and Shinsaibashi.

areas.name: Tezukayama / Kitabatake
areas.short: Old-money Osaka — the classic wealthy residential name.
areas.long: One of the city's best-known luxury areas (Sumiyoshi/Abeno wards): big homes, greenery, private schools.
areas.who: Families and wealthy locals wanting calm and status inside the city.
areas.expect: Leafy streets, detached houses, prestige schools, a genuinely upscale residential feel.

areas.name: Kyobashi / OBP
areas.ja: 京橋・大阪ビジネスパーク
areas.short: Lively, local, great transit — business towers next to old bars.
areas.long: A major junction; OBP is corporate high-rise, Kyobashi station itself is cheap-eats and drinking.
areas.who: People who prize transit access and a lively, unpretentious local scene.
areas.expect: Retro drinking alleys beside glass office towers; convenient, gritty-but-fun, good value.

areas.name: Shin-Osaka
areas.short: Shinkansen gateway — practical, well-connected, not scenic.
areas.long: Built around the bullet-train station; convenient for travel and commuting, light on charm.
areas.who: Frequent travelers and commuters who value connectivity over vibe.
areas.expect: Hotels, offices, easy access everywhere; functional rather than atmospheric.

areas.name: Esaka / Suita
areas.short: Practical, clean, suburban-urban with easy Umeda access.
areas.long: Very livable; Suita groups with northern Osaka's desirable residential areas (e.g. historic Senriyama).
areas.who: People who want more space, safety and comfort over nightlife.
areas.expect: Wide streets, family amenities, direct Midosuji line to Umeda, calmer evenings.

areas.name: Toyonaka / Minoh / Senri-Chuo
areas.ja: 豊中・箕面・千里中央
areas.short: Wealthy northern suburbs — family, nature, quiet.
areas.long: Repeatedly ranked among Osaka's affluent zones (Minoh's Sakurai/Sakuragaoka, Toyonaka's Midorigaoka).
areas.who: Rich families and car owners wanting quiet and green space.
areas.expect: Big houses, good schools, parks and hills; the 'wealthy Osaka' answer outside the core.

areas.name: Higashiyodogawa / Awaji
areas.short: Affordable, local, well-connected by Hankyu lines.
areas.long: Working residential wards north-east of the center; good value, ordinary-Osaka daily life.
areas.who: Budget-minded renters who want cheap rent and solid train access.
areas.expect: Local shopping streets, older apartments, Hankyu lines toward Umeda/Kyoto; plain but practical.

areas.name: Yodogawa / Tsukamoto
areas.short: Cheap, local, one stop from Umeda on the JR loop side.
areas.long: Down-to-earth residential/industrial pockets west of the Yodo river; strong value near the center.
areas.who: Value hunters who want to be close to Umeda for less.
areas.expect: Shitamachi feel, cheap eats, older buildings, quick JR access, not polished.

areas.name: Tamade / Nishinari
areas.short: Cheapest rents in the city — rough reputation, improving.
areas.long: Nishinari has the lowest rents in Osaka; gritty and uneven street-by-street, but central and changing.
areas.who: Very budget-focused renters comfortable with a rough-around-the-edges area.
areas.expect: Bargain rents, local markets, an edgy reputation; check the specific street before committing.

areas.name: Higashisumiyoshi / Tanabe
areas.short: Quiet, local, residential south side — decent value.
areas.long: Ordinary family-residential wards south of Tennoji; calmer and cheaper than the center.
areas.who: Families and long-stay renters wanting quiet and affordability.
areas.expect: Low-rise homes, small shops, parks, easy Tanimachi/Midosuji access south of Tennoji.

areas.name: Tsuruhashi / Imazato / Ikuno
areas.short: Gritty, multicultural east side — Osaka's Koreatown.
areas.long: Ikuno-ku has Japan's biggest Korean community; lively markets, cheap rents, very local.
areas.who: Renters who want cheap, characterful, food-rich neighborhoods off the tourist track.
areas.expect: Tsuruhashi's yakiniku/Korean market, dense older housing, strong local flavor, low prices.

areas.name: Sakai
areas.short: Separate historic city just south — spacious and affordable.
areas.long: Osaka's second city: its own downtown, big parks and the Mozu tombs; cheaper and roomier than the core.
areas.who: People happy to trade central buzz for space, calm and value.
areas.expect: Suburban feel, wide streets, family housing, ~20–30 min by train into central Osaka.
